results.title: ‘My work has always been serious’: Maurizio Cattelan on his $6m banana, his gold toilet – and bringing Hitler to Berlin
results.content:
I wonder, given the death of David Hockney, another epochal figure of the art world, if Cattelan has given any thought to his own legacy, but he does not seem to envision a future in which his work endures. “I don’t have a foundation,” he says. “I don’t have a studio, never had. I also don’t have a family. A legacy would be like being so conscious about yourself that you have these constructions.” [...] Each major exhibition sends him on a rollercoaster of exhilaration and panic, he says, admitting to being “extremely desperate” while planning Night. “Do I suffer? Yes, I don’t like it. It’s always a challenge. I still need the rush. It’s a contradiction, but I love the hate of making a show. It’s a fix. It’s a dependency. Maybe a therapist would say, ‘We can solve your addiction problem.’ And I’d say, ‘No, no, I love it.’” [...] Comedian, 2019, the $6.2m banana. Photograph: © 2025 Maurizio Cattelan

There was also the gold toilet, called America, that was installed in New York’s Guggenheim in 2016, its curators later offering the piece to Donald Trump’s White House instead of the Van Gogh that it requested. Thieves later made off with the 18-carat loo when it went on display at Blenheim Palace, Winston Churchill’s Oxfordshire birthplace.
